correctness.rationale: For p=2 and three distinct active eigenvalues, direct specialization of the published Cauchy--Binet weights leaves exactly one pair at each spectral endpoint. Their quotient gives the stated ratio recurrence. Fixed-weight conjugacy gives the factor w3/w1. Log normalization produces the exact characteristic polynomial with both roots of modulus square-root two. The sign-run argument and linear-recurrence growth establish the zero/infinity subsequences. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

evidence: Yang--Yuan prove broader global R-linear norm convergence and fixed-weight conjugacy for arbitrary active dimension n>p, but do not imply bounded or convergent projective coordinate ratios.

The determinant identity specialized to the minimal nonterminating n=3, p=2 case supplies additional exact cancellation needed for the ratio law.

value.rationale: The three-active-mode p=2 case is the smallest nonterminating LMSD spectral configuration, immediately adjacent to the source finite-termination threshold. The exact closed recurrence identifies a structural phenomenon hidden by norm convergence: all nonfixed projective ratio states have a square-root-two unstable exponent and recurrently approach finite-termination boundary strata. This gives an analytic mechanism for extreme spectral imbalance in a setting where the source reports severe history conditioning while proving global R-linear decay.
